questions.question: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn on, then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: When you start your engine, warning lights and buzzers should come on briefly, then turn off quickly.

questions.question: Look ahead at the road ____ in front of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to see and avoid hazards. Watch for cars entering the highway or changing lanes.

questions.question: When drivers turn, they usually:

options.text: Look in the direction they are turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in the direction they are turning.
questions.explanation: When turning, drivers usually look toward where they are turning. Body movements can show you a driver's intention to turn, even without a signal.

questions.question: After you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off within a few seconds.
Stay on until you turn them off manually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off after a few seconds. If they stay on, something may be wrong with your vehicle.

questions.question: On a slippery road, a driver should:
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, drive slowly and smoothly. Turn gently and do not pass other vehicles unless necessary.

questions.question: If you are not sure if the road is becoming icy, you should:

options.text: Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: Open your window and touch the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice is on them, the road is likely icy too.

questions.question: When pulled over on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Keep your vehicle in front of them.

questions.explanation: Do not react to an aggressive driver's angry gestures. Do not make eye contact. Move away from them if you can do so safely.

questions.question: On hazardous materials shipping papers, the ID number, shipping name, and hazard class should:

options.text: Be shortened if the paper is small.
Be shortened only if the abbreviations are clear.

questions.explanation: The ID number, shipping name, and hazard class must not be shortened on hazardous materials papers, unless the regulations specifically allow it.

questions.question: If you are turning left at an intersection with two left turn lanes, use:

options.text: Either lane — it does not matter.

questions.explanation: Start your left turn in the rightmost left turn lane. You may need to swing right to turn left safely.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle with hazardous materials, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle with hazardous materials. A person must always watch the nozzle and control the fuel flow while refueling.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: Older trailers without spring brakes will lose braking power if the air supply leaks away. What happens?

options.text: The trailer will not have brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will not have brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers without spring brakes have no brakes if the air supply leaks away. The wheels will spin freely with no stopping power.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system can cause what problem?

options.text: Allow poisonous fumes to enter the cabin.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow poisonous fumes to enter the cabin.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can let poisonous fumes into the cabin or sleeper berth. Check your exhaust system regularly for loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: When does alcohol begin to affect the body?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects muscle control, reaction time, depth perception, vision, judgment, and inhibition. For some people, impairment starts with the first drink. Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What must a shipping paper list?

options.text: The location of fire departments along the route.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials shipping papers must list an emergency response telephone number.

questions.question: If brakes pull to one side when used, what does this mean?

options.text: They will be the most effective.

questions.explanation: Brakes that pull to one side when used indicate a brake problem. Have them inspected.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Keeps air in the brake system if a bad leak occurs.
Prevents the trailer from being accidentally released.
Prevents the vehicle from going too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the brake system if a bad leak occurs.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. It closes automatically when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: When loading liquid cargo, what is important to remember?

options.text: There may be construction work along your route.
Too much cargo can slow down your vehicle.
The liquid will expand during transit.

questions.correctAnswerText: The liquid will expand during transit.
questions.explanation: All liquids expand at different rates during transit. Know the expansion rate of your cargo. Consider the liquid's expansion, its weight, and legal weight limits when loading.

questions.question: When turning, when should you signal?

options.text: Turn off the signal just before starting the turn.
Only if vehicles are in front of you.

questions.explanation: Signal well before a turn or lane change. Keep signaling throughout the turn. Cancel the signal after completing the turn, unless your vehicle has self-canceling signals.
